About ProSiteGuide

Clear technology decisions for small law firms

ProSiteGuide explains domains, hosting, email, website platforms and security in plain English, so solo attorneys and small firms can choose with confidence and avoid expensive mistakes.

Start hereWork with me

What firm websites need that blogs don't

  • Confidential inquiriesContact forms collect sensitive details from prospective clients.
  • Reliability when it mattersA site that is down when someone searches is a lost client.
  • No in-house ITMost small firms need tools they can run without a technician.
  • Professional obligationsConfidentiality and advertising rules shape how a firm site works.
Why this site exists

Most tech reviews aren't written for law firms

Hosting and software reviews usually target bloggers and online stores. They rank products on speed tests and introductory prices, then move on.

A law firm's priorities are different. Its website is a first impression, an intake channel and a place where confidential information arrives. Its email must be trustworthy. And when something breaks, there is rarely an IT department to call.

ProSiteGuide covers technology through that lens: what matters for a firm of roughly 1 to 15 lawyers, what it really costs after the introductory price, and how to set it up properly.

Who our guides are for

  • Solo attorneysLaunching a first website or replacing a DIY site.
  • Small firmsChoosing hosting, email and tools that scale with the practice.
  • Office managersKeeping the website, domain and email running day to day.
  • Anyone switching providersMoving hosts or email without downtime or lost messages.
What we cover

Guides for every layer of your firm's online presence

Each guide focuses on one decision, explains the trade-offs and links to official sources so you can check the details yourself.

Domains

Choosing between .com, .law and .attorney, naming your domain and registering it correctly.

Read the guide →

Hosting

Managed WordPress hosting compared on security, backups, support and renewal pricing.

Read the guide →

Business email

Professional domain email with SPF, DKIM and DMARC, plus Google Workspace vs Microsoft 365.

Read the guide →

Website platforms

WordPress, Squarespace and Wix compared for law firm websites.

Read the guide →

Security

A prioritized security checklist and secure contact forms for client inquiries.

Read the guide →

Costs and upkeep

What a law firm website really costs to build and maintain.

Read the guide →
Our principles

How we keep our guides trustworthy

Primary sources

Prices, features and policies come from vendors' official pages, documentation and bar or government sources.

Independent

Affiliate commissions never decide what we recommend or how products are ranked.

Plain English

Technical terms are explained, and every guide ends with practical next steps.

Dated and updated

Guides show when they were last updated, and prices state the month they were checked.

Read how we review products →

Who's behind it

Written by a WordPress developer who builds firm websites

Jayce Tuazon CabangcalaWordPress developer, webmaster and SEO specialist

ProSiteGuide is run by Jayce Tuazon Cabangcala, a WordPress developer with 8+ years of experience and 1,000+ websites delivered, including sites for law firms and mediators. The guides draw on that practical work, combined with careful research into each product's documentation, pricing and terms.

See Jayce's full portfolio at hirejayce.com or connect on LinkedIn.

ProSiteGuide is not a law firm and doesn't give legal advice. When a topic touches professional-conduct rules, such as confidentiality or attorney advertising, we point you to bar association resources and recommend confirming the rules in your state.

See servicesGet in touch

How ProSiteGuide makes money

  • Affiliate linksSome links earn a commission at no extra cost to you. They never change our verdicts.
  • Website servicesThe site's owner offers website design, development and maintenance for law firms.
  • No paid rankingsWe don't sell placements or sponsored reviews.

Read our affiliate disclosure

Questions

About ProSiteGuide

Is ProSiteGuide a law firm?

No. ProSiteGuide publishes technology guides for law firms. Nothing on the site is legal advice, and contacting us does not create an attorney-client relationship.

Do vendors pay to be featured?

No. We don't accept payment for placement or rankings. Some links are affiliate links, which are disclosed and never change our recommendations.

How current are the prices in your guides?

Each guide states when prices were checked. Hosting and software prices change often, so always confirm the current price on the vendor's site before you buy.

Can you help with my firm's website?

Yes. ProSiteGuide offers website builds, migrations, email setup and maintenance for law firms. See services.

How do I report an error in a guide?

Use the contact form or email prositeguidejayce@gmail.com. Every correction request is reviewed.

New to all of this?

Follow our step-by-step path from domain to launch.

Start here Contact us
